# Local continuation of the detuned hard-core pair

## Statement and scope

All operators below are the exact semi-infinite ladder in the supplied
packet, in its two-excitation sector, at the fixed coupling (g=1/5).
Write (H_eta=H_g+eta V), (V=n_L-n_R), and let (E,psi) be the
normalized even hard-core pair in the supplied construction. Put

\[
 s(z)=\langle V\psi,(H_{g,\mathrm{odd}}-z)^{-1}V\psi\rangle,
 \qquad \operatorname{Im}z>0.
\]

The following is a local mathematical resonance theorem for this actual
perturbation. It does not require (V) to have finite rank on the
two-particle space.

**Theorem.** There are (r>0), (epsilon>0), and a continuation from the
upper half-plane of both

\[
 G_p(\eta,z)=\langle LR,(H_\eta-z)^{-1}LR\rangle,
 \qquad
 G_\psi(\eta,z)=\langle\psi,(H_\eta-z)^{-1}\psi\rangle
\]

to meromorphic functions on (D(E,r)), for real (|\eta|<\epsilon).
They have the same unique simple pole (lambda(\eta)) there, and their
residues in the convention (a(\eta)/(\lambda(\eta)-z)) are nonzero.
The pole and its projection are holomorphic in complex (eta) near zero,
and the pole is even:

\[
 \boxed{\lambda(\eta)=E-s(E+i0)\eta^2+O(\eta^4).} \tag{1}
\]

In particular, for real (eta), the density proved in the supplied
`S62/PROOF.md` gives

\[
 \boxed{\operatorname{Im}\lambda(\eta)
       =-\pi\rho_g(E)\eta^2+O(\eta^4),\qquad \rho_g(E)>0.} \tag{2}
\]

Thus the pole is strictly in the lower half-plane for all sufficiently
small nonzero real detunings. The constants (r,epsilon) are specified
constructively by resolvent conditions in §7; no useful numerical lower
bound for (epsilon) is asserted. The displayed density decimal remains
uncertified. This theorem is neither an all-times exponential survival law
nor a hardware lifetime or gate-error estimate.

# ASTRA foundational physics — symmetry-resolved embedded pairs with nonzero coherent interaction

27 October 2026. Independent continuation of the embedded two-photon SSH resonance. Units: \(\hbar=B=1\). This note records exact mathematical statements for an explicit local Hamiltonian, finite-chain executable checks, the original route that fails to give an exact bound state, and a deliberate counterconstruction in which radiation protection **also cancels the interaction**. No external novelty, experimental platform, or practical gate advantage is asserted.

## 1. Choice of mechanism

The preceding SSH gradient-port model had a pair resonance with a nonzero connected shift \(\chi=-g^4/12+o(g^4)\) and an eighth-order radiative linewidth \(\Gamma=(43/(5184\pi))g^8+o(g^8)\). Its two-photon radiation coefficient was a **sum of nonnegative parity-channel spectral convolutions**. Changing emitter spacing did not remove the shell contribution. One option is to prove finite-coupling resonance-error estimates. A higher-upside alternative is to **filter the one-photon bath bands by symmetry**: make each emitter-parity channel see only one side of the one-photon gap. Then the pair remains embedded in the *full* two-photon continuum but is spectrally isolated in its invariant symmetry sector. We construct this alternative.

## 2. One connected, nearest-neighbour, real-hopping ladder

There are two hard-core memory sites \(L,R\) and two semi-infinite oscillator rails \(A_j,B_j\), \(j=0,1,\dots\). Each memory has excitation energy 3. Each rail oscillator has energy 3, neighbouring sites in a rail hop with amplitude \(-1/2\), and corresponding sites across rails have real rung hopping \(+2\). Thus the bath has no direct connection between different distant rail sites other than local leg and rung edges.

The physical two-memory space excludes \(|LL\rangle\) and \(|RR\rangle\), but contains \(|LR\rangle\); no harmonic approximation is made to the two memories.

# Local parity-breaking response of the hard-core ladder

## Statement and scope

For the semi-infinite ladder in the supplied source, at **exactly** \(g=1/5\), let \(\psi_g\) be the normalized dressed even hard-core pair and let \(V=n_L-n_R\). Then

\[
\rho(E_p)=\frac1\pi\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
\operatorname{Im}\langle V\psi_g,(H_{\rm odd}-E_p-i\epsilon)^{-1}V\psi_g\rangle
\]

exists and satisfies

\[
\boxed{0<\rho(E_p)<\infty.}
\]

An explicit continuum expression is (14) below. Its evaluation gives
\(\rho(E_p)\simeq2.12750672\times10^{-8}\) in the declared units. This decimal is a numerical quadrature result. Separately, an outward-rounded interval computation using only algebraic atoms, support bounds and two continuum intervals proves
\(\rho(E_p)>4\times10^{-16}\); it does not assume accuracy of that quadrature.

The consequence is a nonzero local symmetry-breaking transition coefficient for the actual protected pair at fixed nonzero coupling. The exact available machinery is the source's even pair resolvent together with the explicit half-line Jacobi measures. The missing link addressed here is the *dressed source and complete odd hard-core compression*. The strongest operational alternative already in the source is exact preservation of the exchange parity; a parity-preserving wrong-band source is a different perturbation and supplies no coefficient for this \(V\).

Only the supplied `ASTRA_SYMMETRY_FILTERED_EMBEDDED_PAIR_20261027.md` and its two supplied Python constructions are used as scientific input, frozen under source revision `c1b8ac1516457a88b383a6350680e3be865fbffd`. No novelty or physical-device claim is made.

## Complete one-body measures

Use the convention
\(r_\sigma(z)=\langle e_\sigma,(h_\sigma-z)^{-1}e_\sigma\rangle\), so its upper boundary value has nonnegative imaginary part. Write

\[
 c_+=5,\quad c_-=1,\qquad k_+=2g^2,\quad k_-=g^2,
\]

where \(k_\sigma\) is the **square** of the endpoint coupling. Define

\[
 q_c(z)=2[-(z-c)+\sqrt{z-c-1}\sqrt{z-c+1}],\qquad
 r_\sigma(z)=\frac1{3-z-k_\sigma q_{c_\sigma}(z)}. \tag{1}
\]

Both square roots are principal for \(\operatorname{Im}z>0\); their product is asymptotic to \(z-c\). This fixes all signs and branches. The memory endpoint is cyclic for each irreducible Jacobi matrix, so its spectral representation is the complete one-body space, not a selected bath mode.

statement: The physical relative-memory detuning couples the dressed pair to a finite strictly positive odd hard-core continuum at g=1/5. A separate interval argument certifies rho>4e-16; the approximate 2.12750672e-8 decimal is not certified.
